title: Pi RPC provider (SPEC §9): argv builder, findings-extension.ts (submit_findings tool), JSONL event loop, env passthrough, corrective-prompt retries, heartbeat watchdog, version probe + graceful no-detector degradation
description:
Implement the Pi RPC provider — the single transport through which facts are produced. DELIVERABLES: src/investigation/provider/ exposes investigate(repoPath, area, opts): Promise (SPEC §9.0 core entrypoint). buildPiArgv mirrors burrow (../burrow/src/runtime/pi.ts reference): pi --mode rpc --no-session --no-extensions -e --offline --no-context-files --provider

--model --tools ,submit_findings --system-prompt , cwd = target repo. src/investigation/provider/pi/findings-extension.ts registers the submit_findings tool whose parameter JSON-schema derives from the area's zod schema via zod-to-json-schema. Protocol per SPEC §9.3: write one prompt line, HOLD STDIN OPEN, watch stdout JSONL for the submit_findings toolCall, zod-validate arguments, close stdin on capture; on missing/invalid call send one corrective prompt echoing zod errors, bounded to N retries (default 2); exhaustion/timeout/stopReason:error → resolve no-detector with the failure rationale, never a fabricated pass. Heartbeat watchdog force-terminates stalls. Provider/model selection precedence: CLI flags > targets.yaml defaults.investigation > one documented constant; provider names lowercased. Env passthrough only (never argv): ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/AUTH_TOKEN/BASE_URL always + the PI_PROVIDER_ENV_KEYS map (openai/google/groq/mistral/deepseek) per §9.4. Startup probe: pi --version against the documented supported version; missing/incompatible Pi degrades every agent criterion to no-detector with a hint — never crashes the audit. DELIVERABLE TESTS: argv construction, env filtering, retry/corrective flow, watchdog, and degradation — all against a scripted fake pi process (no live calls). ACCEPTANCE: bun test green with zero network/model access. REFERENCES: SPEC §9.0-9.6.

DELIVERABLES: src/investigation/__golden__/ holds one captured real `pi --mode rpc` session per area (full JSONL event stream including the submit_findings toolCall), canonicalized — timestamps, responseId, session/tool-call ids, usage normalized to fixed placeholders — and frozen. A capture/regeneration script (scripts/ or test helper) re-records goldens ONLY when TRELLIS_UPDATE_PI_GOLDEN=1 AND an explicit live-call flag are both set; otherwise it refuses. Unit tests run the full chain offline: RPC parser → toolCall capture → zod validation → deterministic grader, asserting the exact grades each golden produces; a corrupted-golden fixture exercises the corrective/no-detector path. CI configuration makes no model calls anywhere (assert via test that no network env is required). ACCEPTANCE: bun test green offline with PI/API env vars unset; regeneration script documented in AGENTS.md/RUNBOOK; goldens stable across two consecutive test runs. NOTE: the initial capture requires one live Pi run per area by the operator — coordinate with the user if no capture exists yet; until then hand-authored fixtures matching the real wire shape (validated against burrow's documented v0.74.0 envelope) are acceptable and marked as such. REFERENCES: SPEC §9.7, burrow golden methodology.

title: Wire investigation into audit: investigate() core entrypoint, investigation_cache keyed (repo, commit_sha, area), --no-cache flag, agent criteria flow into the scorecard
description: Wire the investigation layer into the audit pipeline with caching. DELIVERABLES: the audit core, for each of the 4 areas referenced by any to-be-scored agent criterion, resolves findings via: investigation_cache lookup keyed (repo, commit_sha, area) → on miss, investigate() (Pi provider) → zod-validate → cache write; --no-cache forces re-investigation (SPEC §7.3/§9.5). Grader output for all 20 agent criteria flows into the scorecard alongside deterministic results; rationale strings name the area + key facts. Areas run once per repo per commit regardless of how many criteria consume them (bounded LLM cost). Pi-unavailable or area-failure paths surface as no-detector entries counted against coverage. commit_sha resolution: git rev-parse HEAD of the target; dirty worktrees recorded with a -dirty suffix so cache keys never lie. DELIVERABLE TESTS: cache hit/miss/no-cache flows against a temp DB with a stubbed provider; an end-to-end audit of a fixture repo where agent criteria score from cached findings, asserting byte-identical scorecards across two runs at the same commit. ACCEPTANCE: bun test green; `trellis audit` on a fixture exercises det + agent criteria together; re-run at same commit is byte-identical. REFERENCES: SPEC §7.3, §9.5, §3.2.

title: Canonical standards set: src/standards/canonical/ files extracted from the l5-toolkit/warren conventions + manifest.yaml with per-file semver, hashes, and matcher kinds (SPEC §10)
description: Author the canonical standards set and manifest. DELIVERABLES: src/standards/canonical/ contains the bundled canonical files per SPEC §10, extracted from the current os-eco conventions (templates/l5-toolkit + warren as reference): biome.json, tsconfig.base.json, .github/workflows/ci.yml, AGENTS.md (template/section-aware), scripts/hooks/pre-commit, .seeds/config.yaml — plus any additional files the l5-toolkit treats as canonical (knip.json, .jscpd.json, bunfig.toml, dependabot.yml) where stable. src/standards/manifest.yaml describes the set: top-level version (start "1.0.0"), and per file { path, version, hash: sha256, matcher: exact|json-subset|yaml-subset|text|template }. A small script or test recomputes hashes so manifest drift inside trellis itself fails CI. DELIVERABLE TESTS: manifest schema validation (zod), hash agreement between manifest.yaml and the canonical files on disk, matcher kind coverage. ACCEPTANCE: bun test green; `trellis standards` (landing next step) will read this manifest; every canonical file is byte-tracked. REFERENCES: SPEC §10, templates/l5-toolkit/configs+github, warren root configs.

title: Drift engine: drift.ts matchers (exact/json-subset/yaml-subset/text/template), allowed-deltas, per-file states (match/allowed-delta/drift/missing/extra), trellis drift + trellis standards commands, report.drift
description: Implement the drift engine and its CLI commands. DELIVERABLES: src/standards/drift.ts compares a target repo against the canonical set: per-file matchers exact (byte), json-subset (canonical keys must be present/equal, target may extend), yaml-subset, text (normalized whitespace), template (section-aware for AGENTS.md — required sections present, boilerplate matched); per-file output state match | allowed-delta | drift | missing | extra. Allowed deltas honor the targets.yaml shape (file-level and structural paths within a file, each with a reason) — whitelisted divergences report allowed-delta, not drift. The target's tracked canonical version resolves per-repo override > defaults.canonicalVersion. `trellis drift <repo-path>` runs drift standalone (accepts --canonical <v>; without fleet context allowedDeltas default empty); `trellis standards` prints the canonical manifest + versions. Drift results fold into the audit report under report.drift (SPEC §6.3). DELIVERABLE TESTS: fixture repos per matcher kind and per state (match/allowed/drift/missing/extra), structural-path allow-listing, version override resolution. ACCEPTANCE: bun test green; `trellis drift` on a warren-stack checkout produces a coherent per-file table in terminal/JSON/MD. REFERENCES: SPEC §10, §6.5, §12.

title: Fleet: targets.yaml loader (defaults, per-target canonical overrides + allowedDeltas, skip, osecoDetectors, languages) + trellis fleet multi-repo orchestration
description: Implement fleet orchestration. DELIVERABLES: src/fleet/ loads and zod-validates targets.yaml per SPEC §6.5: defaults { canonicalVersion, investigation.{provider,model} } and targets[] { id, path, languages?, canonical?: { version?, allowedDeltas? }, skip?: criterion ids forced to not-applicable, osecoDetectors?: boolean }. Path resolution relative to the targets.yaml location; missing/unreadable target paths fail that target with a clear per-target error without aborting the fleet. `trellis fleet [--targets targets.yaml] [--json|--md]` audits every target sequentially (audit + drift with the target's allowedDeltas and skip list applied), persists each run to the central store, and renders an aggregate dashboard: per-repo level, pass rate, coverage, drift counts, and level deltas vs each repo's previous run. The skip list maps to not-applicable with rationale 'skipped via targets.yaml'. DELIVERABLE TESTS: targets schema validation fixtures, skip/osecoDetectors/allowedDeltas plumbing into the audit context, partial-failure isolation, aggregate rendering snapshot. ACCEPTANCE: bun test green; a two-fixture-target fleet run writes two runs rows and prints the aggregate table. REFERENCES: SPEC §6.5, §12, §14.7.

title: History reporting: trellis report dashboard from SQLite (--repo/--since/--json/--md) + changes-since-last-run deltas with rubric-version attribution (SPEC §11)
description: Implement history reporting and change attribution. DELIVERABLES: `trellis report [--repo <id>] [--since <date>] [--json|--md]` renders from the central SQLite store: per-repo run history (level, pass rate, coverage over time), fleet snapshot of latest runs, and per-criterion trend queries powered by criterion_results. changesSinceLastRun (SPEC §11): comparing a run against the most recent prior run for the same repo, list per-criterion transitions (pass→fail, fail→pass, naKind changes, app-count/denominator changes) and the net level move; embed in the §6.3 report at audit time and render in `trellis report`. Rubric attribution: when the two runs' rubric_version differ, the delta is flagged explicitly as possibly-rubric-driven; identical versions mark it a real code regression/improvement. DELIVERABLE TESTS: seeded multi-run temp DBs asserting delta computation across all transition kinds, the rubric-version flag both ways, --since filtering, and renderer snapshots. ACCEPTANCE: bun test green; after two fleet runs of a changed fixture, `trellis report` shows the criterion-level diff with correct attribution. REFERENCES: SPEC §11, §6.3, §6.4, §12.

title: os-eco-native detectors (SPEC §8.4): seeds/mulch/canopy/plot/skills/check:all/ratchet evidence mapped onto existing criteria, osecoDetectors per-target toggle
description: Implement the os-eco-native detector pack in src/detectors/oseco/. DELIVERABLES: evidence detectors that strengthen EXISTING criteria (no new category, SPEC §8.4), active by default and disabled when the target sets osecoDetectors: false: AGENTS.md+CLAUDE.md richness → agents_md; */SKILL.md → skills; .seeds/ presence + labeling config (+ sd data when available) → issue_templates / issue_labeling_system / backlog_health; check:all script + CI invoking it verbatim → unit_tests_runnable / pre_commit_hooks / fast_ci_feedback evidence; ratchet scripts (file-size/debt/coverage/complexity/bundle/jscpd/knip) → large_file_detection / tech_debt_tracking / code_quality_metrics / dead_code_detection / duplicate_code_detection / unused_dependencies_detection / heavy_dependency_detection; gen:openapi + docs/openapi.yaml → api_schema_docs; gen:docs → automated_doc_generation; .canopy/ → automated_doc_generation evidence; .mulch/ → documentation_freshness / agentic_development; .plot/ → agentic_development; agent co-author trailers in git log → agentic_development. Composition rule: oseco evidence merges with (never replaces) the common/language detector verdicts — pass if either passes; rationale names the oseco evidence path. DELIVERABLE TESTS: fixture repos with/without each surface, the toggle, and merge semantics. ACCEPTANCE: bun test green; auditing a warren-stack fixture with the pack on measurably raises honest pass rates vs off. REFERENCES: SPEC §8.4, §6.5.

title: Typed SDK (src/client/) mirroring core types + CLI exit-code contract (--fail-on level|gate|drift|none) so trellis is CI-usable per repo (SPEC §12, §13.1)
description: Ship the typed SDK and the CI-usable exit-code contract. DELIVERABLES: src/client/ exports a typed programmatic client (SPEC §13.1): audit(repoPath, opts), drift(repoPath, opts), fleet(targetsPath, opts), report(query), rubric() — each calling the SAME core functions the CLI does, in-process, with request/response types that mirror the core's exported types (annotated // Mirrors src/<x>). No logic in the SDK beyond type shaping. Exit-code contract across all CLI commands (SPEC §12): 0 clean; non-zero when a gate criterion fails or drift is detected, tunable via --fail-on level|gate|drift|none (document the default; level compares against a --min-level threshold). Sync enforcement: golden snapshots of the stable output shapes (report JSON, drift JSON) live in tests so surface drift turns CI red; strict tsc over the mirrored types. DELIVERABLE TESTS: SDK and CLI invocations of the same audit produce deep-equal reports (one code path proof); each --fail-on mode's exit code asserted via spawned CLI on fixtures. ACCEPTANCE: bun test + check:all green; README/AGENTS.md document the SDK entrypoints and exit codes. REFERENCES: SPEC §12, §13.1.

title: Dogfood gate: trellis audits itself (must band L4+) and the warren-stack fleet end-to-end; iterate detector bindings on what actually mattered
description: Run the dogfood gate. DELIVERABLES: a real targets.yaml at the operator's machine paths covering trellis itself + the warren-stack repos (warren, burrow, plot, mulch, seeds, canopy, sapling); `trellis fleet` completes end-to-end (deterministic + cached investigation criteria + drift + oseco pack); `trellis audit .` on trellis itself bands L4 or higher — if it doesn't, file and fix the honest gaps in trellis's own repo standards (this step includes that remediation) or fix dishonest detectors. Iterate detector bindings on what the fleet run teaches: every no-detector result is triaged into (a) detector bug → fix, (b) genuinely missing adapter → leave counted, or (c) honestly absent surface → reclassify not-applicable; record decisions via ml record. Two consecutive fleet runs at unchanged commits must be byte-identical per repo (determinism check at fleet scale). DELIVERABLES (artifacts): the triage notes land as seeds issues or mulch records; detector fixes land as commits with tests. ACCEPTANCE: trellis self-audit ≥ L4; fleet dashboard renders all targets; check:all green; the SPEC §14 dogfood gate is closed. REFERENCES: SPEC §13 (dogfood mandate), §14 (gate).

title: Release v0.1.0: CHANGELOG roll, version sync (package.json + src VERSION), publish @os-eco/trellis-cli via the version-gated workflow

Verify the publish path: workflows/publish.yml is version-gated against npm view @os-eco/trellis-cli (package not yet on npm → publishes on first main push once NPM_TOKEN is configured; coordinate with the operator for the token — see ../scripts/set-npm-token.sh at the os-eco root). title: Audit run observability + report file export (--output)
description:
`trellis audit .` is a black box while running and the default terminal output is too brief to act on. Two parts:

## 1. Live progress indication

The audit runs 0.5–10min (investigation pass: up to 4 areas x ~2min Pi RPC sessions each) with zero output until the final report. Surface phase-level progress on stderr:

- Phase transitions in auditRepo (src/report/build.ts:329): app discovery -> investigation -> detectors -> scoring.
- Investigation events in runInvestigation (src/investigation/run.ts:145): per-area start, cache hit vs miss, Pi version probe, agent session start/end, retry attempts. Pi session loop (src/investigation/provider/pi/session.ts:263) already sees message_end/agent_end/heartbeat events — wire them to an optional progress callback in InvestigationDeps rather than logging directly from core.
- Per-app detector pass progress (src/report/build.ts:368).
- CLI: default to concise human progress lines on stderr (TTY-aware); add --quiet to suppress and --verbose for per-detector/per-message detail. Adopt the existing-but-unused pino logger (src/cli/logger.ts:16) or a thin progress-reporter interface owned by cli/ so core stays surface-agnostic (api>cli>sdk discipline — core emits events, CLI renders them).

## 2. Report file export

All three renderers (terminal/JSON/markdown) exist but emit() (src/cli/output.ts:84) writes stdout only. Add:

- --output <path> on audit: writes the report to a file. Format inferred from extension (.json -> renderJson, .md -> renderMarkdown), overridable by --json/--md. Terminal summary still prints to stdout so the run remains readable.
- Keep stdout contract stable for piping (progress goes to stderr, never stdout).
- SDK: mirror the option in client/ per the mirroring convention.

Out of scope: enriching the default terminal report detail (separate concern), HTTP surface.

Touch points: src/cli/audit.ts:28 (AuditCliOptions), src/cli/output.ts, src/report/build.ts, src/report/run.ts:48, src/investigation/run.ts, src/investigation/provider/pi/session.ts, src/client/.

title: Make markdown/json report file render the full audit (terminal stays brief)
description:
Refines the original enrich-report ask after dogfooding feedback. DECISION: the terminal/TUI scorecard (src/report/terminal.ts) is good as-is and should NOT get richer — leave the level banner + per-category table + N/A tally untouched, no --detail flag for terminal. The gap is the persisted report FILE: src/report/markdown.ts (37 lines) only mirrors the terminal aggregates, so the written report is useless for acting on a score (you cannot see which of the 90 criteria passed/failed/why). Make the markdown (and confirm json) FILE output render literally everything the audit looked at and graded — maximal detail, no flag, always full.

Markdown must render, grouped by category with failing criteria surfaced first:
- every criterion: id, title, category, verdict (pass/fail/n-a vs no-detector via naKind), numerator/denominator
- the per-criterion rationale string (the WHY, =500 chars) from ScorecardEntry
- which gate criterion(s) failed (e.g. single_command_setup) via failingGateIds/gateFails (src/report/assess.ts, src/scoring/gate.ts) — currently only on stderr
- report.drift (canonical-config drift) and report.changesSinceLastRun (per-criterion transitions) — present on the object, never rendered

JSON: src/report/json.ts is JSON.stringify(report) so it already carries report.criteria + drift + changes; verify nothing detailed is dropped and keep it complete. Data is fully available today (report.criteria: Record<string,ScorecardEntry>, src/report/types.ts:48; entry shape src/scoring/entry.ts:27-32) — this is purely a renderer gap, no new collection needed. Touch points: src/report/markdown.ts, src/report/rollup.ts (may need a per-criterion projection helper), src/report/types.ts, golden snapshots. Out of scope: terminal changes, remediation hints.

title: CLI tests litter the real repo .trellis/ — default report output is cwd-relative
description:
Symptom: after running bun test, the real repo's .trellis/ fills with timestamped audit-*.md reports (25 observed). These are NOT from a user audit run — each file's H1 names a test temp dir (trellis-cli-exit-*, trellis-cli-audit-*, trellis-sdk-*).

Root cause (two parts):
1. src/cli/audit.ts planReportTarget (~lines 167-181, added in commit ca3e99d): when --output is omitted, the DEFAULT report target is join(process.cwd(), '.trellis') — anchored to the CURRENT WORKING DIRECTORY, not the audited repo path, and not disabled. Filenames are audit-<scoredAt-to-the-second>.md (finalizeReportPath ~185-189), so runs on different seconds accumulate instead of overwriting (N runs = N files).
2. The CLI/SDK tests spawn 'trellis audit <tempdir>' WITHOUT setting cwd and WITHOUT --no-output, so the child inherits the real trellis repo root as cwd and writes into its .trellis/. Offenders: src/cli/exit-codes.test.ts (spawn has no cwd ~21-25; auditCli helper omits --no-output ~57-62; ~8 audit calls), src/cli/main.test.ts (~233-314), src/client/index.test.ts (~60). .gitignore:29 ignores .trellis/, so the pollution is invisible to git.

Note: a single user 'trellis audit . --output .' correctly writes exactly ONE file (to cwd); it does not loop. The pile-up is purely test fallout.

Fix options to weigh during design: (a) make tests set cwd to a temp dir and/or pass --no-output; (b) make the default report-output anchor to the audited repo path, not process.cwd(); (c) gate default file export behind a flag / env so tests don't trigger it; (d) clean up the existing 25 stray .trellis/ files. Pick during design — at minimum tests must not write into the real repo.

title: Factory-ready verdict: warren dispatchability detector pack + top-line DISPATCHABLE yes/no
description: Add detectors/oseco/warren.ts answering the binary question 'can warren dispatch against this repo today?'. Checks (all deterministic, from warren's real dispatch contract): .warren/config.yaml parses against warren's DefaultsConfigSchema (vendor or import the zod schema so trellis and warren can never disagree); qualityGate names a script that actually exists in package.json/Makefile (without it warren agents fall back to fuzzy CLAUDE.md heuristics); .seeds/ present (mandatory for plan-run dispatch); git hooks wired via prepare script core.hooksPath; default branch resolvable; runBranchPrefix/branch conventions sane. Report gains a top-line DISPATCHABLE: yes/no verdict with blocking reasons, separate from the scored rubric (an external repo must be able to hit L5 without os-eco). Lives behind the existing osecoDetectors flag.

pivotDisposition.reason: The os-eco detector overlay and readiness verdict are retired. Warren dispatchability is outside the deterministic measurement release; any future separate capability needs a new bounded proposal.

title: Exec tier: trellis runs the declared quality gate and measures verify-loop wall-clock
description: trellis currently only inspects; it should also execute. Opt-in exec tier (trellis audit --exec or a verify profile) that runs the repo's declared quality gate (.warren qualityGate, or the detected verify/check:all entrypoint), records pass/fail + wall-clock duration, and persists both in run history so trellis report shows verify-loop latency per repo over time. Makes the README credo 'any change is verifiable in under 60 seconds' an actual measured criterion instead of a slogan. Execution must run whatever gate the repo declares (never hardcode bun run check:all) to stay tool-agnostic. Support sandboxed execution via burrow when available (see runtime-smoke issue) and bare subprocess otherwise; degrade to no-detector, never false-fail, when execution is unavailable.

pivotDisposition.reason: Running target quality gates and timing verification is explicitly deferred by SPEC 15. No --exec surface or project-command execution is authorized by pl-b2ea.

title: Runtime smoke verification: rubric criterion + execution in burrow/warren and local verify scripts
description: The #1 fleet-wide gap found in the 14-repo scout sweep (mulch, canopy, kota-memory, kota-face, kota-voice all flagged it): gates prove code lints/typechecks/unit-tests but nothing proves the artifact actually runs — daemon boots, /health responds, CLI installs and executes, UI builds and renders. Two halves: (1) new rubric criterion (runtime_smoke_verification or similar, tool-agnostic WHAT: 'the canonical gate includes booting the built artifact and verifying liveness') graded by detectors that look for smoke steps wired into the declared verify/check:all chain; (2) an execution path — trellis (and warren runs) can execute the smoke step inside a burrow sandbox so 'does it run' is verified in isolation, both in the factory loop and locally. Pairs with the exec-tier issue; this is the criterion + sandbox story, that one is the runner + timing story.

pivotDisposition.reason: Project smoke execution and a new readiness criterion are outside SPEC 8/15. trellis-7203 tests this package itself; audits only inspect target safeguard configuration. Re-scope before future execution work.

title: trellis sync: turn audit failures and drift into seeds issues / warren plans (SPEC §15)
description: The missing 'sync' half of 'audit & sync'. A new command (trellis sync or audit --emit-issues) that converts failed criteria and canonical-drift findings into seeds issues (or a seeds plan) in the target repo — criterion id, rationale, and remediation hint in the body — sized for autonomous work. run-plan.sh or warren plan-run dispatch then closes the loop: audit -> issues -> dispatch -> PR -> re-audit shows the level move. Drift findings are the easiest first cut (each drifted canonical file is one mechanical PR). Needs idempotency: re-running sync must not duplicate open issues (key on criterion id + rubric version).

pivotDisposition.reason: Automatic issue filing, dispatch and remediation are outside SPEC 15 and the zero-footprint default. A later explicit opt-in design must use versioned findings, not rubric criteria or maturity levels.

title: Canonical standards v2: adopt kota-monorepo frozen contracts into standards/ and the rubric
description: trellis's bundled standards/ derive from warren-era L5 toolkit; the kota fleet has evolved past it with frozen, machine-verified contracts (kota-monorepo docs/check-all-standard.md and docs/observability-standard.md). Rev canonical standards to v2: ordered GATES manifest pattern (scripts/check-all.ts with exported GATES array as single source of truth), check:ci-parity (CI may invoke nothing outside the manifest), check:boundaries (dependency-cruiser layering as hard errors), check:secrets (gitleaks), golden contract locks (check:openapi byte-diff pattern), per-incident runbooks (kota-memory ships six playbooks), and the 7-rule observability/silent-failure contract. Add matching tool-agnostic rubric criteria (ci-parity enforced, boundary enforcement, contract golden locks, runbooks per failure mode, mutation testing ratchet, test quarantine with tracker links). Dogfood consequence: trellis itself must adopt v2 to keep its L4+ self-score.

pivotDisposition.reason: Standards expansion is excluded by SPEC 11. Existing canonical drift stays separate and unscored; rubric additions and the L4+ dogfood requirement are superseded. A future standards proposal must use the new contract.

title: Rubric ceiling policy: no repo scores 100% — rev the rubric when the fleet tops out
description: Policy + mechanism: a 100% score means the rubric is behind the fleet, not that the repo is done. (1) Document the policy in SPEC/README: the rubric is a ratchet on the whole fleet; when any audited repo passes every measured criterion, that is the trigger to add criteria / tighten bands in the next RUBRIC_VERSION. (2) Mechanize the signal: trellis fleet / trellis report flag any repo at 100% pass-rate (or all-gates-passing at L5) with an explicit 'rubric ceiling reached — rev the rubric' warning, and the history store should make ceiling events queryable so the dashboard surfaces them. Keeps levels meaningful as the fleet improves.

pivotDisposition.reason: Readiness ceiling/L5 policy conflicts with the lower-is-better structural index; zero debt is valid. Formula saturation research remains trellis-831b and requires evidence plus a scoring-version bump.

closeReason: Readiness ceiling/L5 policy conflicts with the lower-is-better structural index; zero debt is valid. Formula saturation research remains trellis-831b and requires evidence plus a scoring-version bump.

description: src/report/build.oseco.test.ts 'the pack on raises honest pass rates vs off (acceptance)' runs a real auditRepo twice and intermittently exceeds bun's default 5s per-test timeout on GitHub-hosted runners (failed the v0.1.0 publish run 27323397867 first attempt; passed the parallel CI run on the same commit and passes locally). Fix: raise the per-test timeout for this acceptance test (bun test supports a timeout arg per test) or slim the fixture so two full audit passes fit comfortably; also killed '1 dangling process' was logged — check the test leaves no subprocess behind. Per canonical-standards-v2 direction (trellis-79c9), a recurring flake should land in a tracked quarantine pattern, not be retried blindly.

title: Detectors fingerprint named tools and miss in-house implementations (false negatives on kota-memory)
description: Fleet baseline 2026-06-11: kota-memory fails feature_flag_infrastructure with rationale 'no feature-flag system (LaunchDarkly/Unleash/OpenFeature/Flipt/...) configured' — but it has a documented, runtime-toggleable in-house flag system (KM_FEATURE_<NAME> env overrides + config, src/flags). Same pattern for structured_logging ('0/1 apps pass' — kota-memory ships an in-house zero-dep structured JSON logger per its dependency charter, no pino/winston fingerprint). The rubric WHAT is tool-agnostic but these detectors only recognize product fingerprints, so zero-dep/in-house implementations (the entire kota charter) read as absent. Fix direction: per-criterion fallback heuristics (env-var flag pattern + config docs; JSON-lines logger usage) and/or route to the investigation pass when deterministic fingerprints miss — a fact like 'repo implements X in-house' must grade pass. Also verify kota-memory's secrets_management fail ('Secrets are committed') — possibly fixture/allowlist false positive from the investigation grader.

Preserve the false-negative lesson for trellis-b412 and trellis-8ac1; do not expand the retained legacy adapters.

Preserve the false-negative lesson for trellis-b412 and trellis-8ac1; do not expand the retained legacy adapters.

title: Investigate run-to-run score variance: kota-memory 94% vs 90% pass across back-to-back audits
description: During the 2026-06-11 fleet baseline kota-memory scored 94% pass on one run and 90% on the fleet run shortly after (same day; commit likely unchanged). Investigation results are cached keyed (repo, commit_sha, area), so two same-commit runs should be identical — either the commit differed, the cache was bypassed, or the Pi investigation pass is nondeterministic across cache misses. ## Design input from trellis-5a91 (feasibility decision, recorded in SPEC §5.3)

**Algorithm/library**: own normalized-token clone detector over the shared syntax inventory (trellis-d81d) — no new runtime dependency. Per file, walk the shared `ts.SourceFile` and collect leaf tokens in document order (NOT a raw `ts.createScanner` loop: it mis-tokenizes template literals without manual re-scan state — reproduced in the spike). Normalize: every identifier → one placeholder, every literal (string, numeric, bigint, regex, template part) → one placeholder, all other tokens keep their `SyntaxKind`. Hash sliding windows of K=50 normalized tokens; extend equal windows from distinct positions into maximal matches; group by content identity of the maximal normalized sequence (drop same-file token-contained members; no transitive merging). Minimum clone: 50 tokens AND 3 lines (provisional, trellis-e924 calibrates). Detection runs per source set (production and test separately; never cross-set); generated/vendored/declaration-only/excluded files are not tokenized. Numerator = union of code-classified lines inside member ranges counted once per file; denominator = scope code-classified lines. Budgets on token count and match work trip `incomplete`, never a silent clean result.

**Expected clone fixture outputs at K=50** (hand-authored fixtures; spike-verified 2026-09-16):
- `exact` (identical function in 2 files): 1 group, members a.ts 4-15 + b.ts 4-15; 22 unique duplicated code lines of 27.
- `renamed` (identifiers + literals renamed, structure identical): 1 group, members a.ts 1-15 + b.ts 1-15; density 1.0. (jscpd 4/5 miss this in default mode.)
- `overlap` (a.ts = regions X+Y, b.ts = Y+Z, c.ts = X+Y+Z): 2 groups — (a.ts 2-16, c.ts 2-16) and (b.ts 2-16, c.ts 10-24); c.ts's lines counted once in the union (49 unique lines of 49).
- `multicopy` (same 9-line function in 4 files): 1 group with 4 members (a/b/c/d.ts 1-9).
- `short` (shared ~30-token idiom): 0 groups at K=50 (below threshold).
- `near` (2 of 9 lines changed): 1 group covering only the maximal shared run (a.ts 7-13, b.ts 3-9); the divergent tail is not merged (type-3 out of scope).

Note: member line ranges are token-exact maximal runs and may overhang a partial boundary line (e.g. `exact` starts at line 4, the trailing `;`/`}` of a preceding statement) — both jscpd engines behave identically; this is accepted semantics, fixtures should assert it.

title: Path-mapped non-TS asset imports (e.g. '@/index.css') are reported unresolved and degrade import-cycle scoring to worst case
description:
Observed auditing warren (2026-09-16): src/ui/src/main.tsx:4 imports '@/index.css'. The file exists at src/ui/src/index.css, but the audit emits graph.unresolved-import ('matches a tsconfig path mapping but resolved to no file').

Root cause: src/metrics/graph-resolve.ts resolveEdge() asks the TS module resolver, which only resolves TS/JS/JSON extensions. A path-mapped specifier that names a non-TS asset (.css, .svg, .png, ...) returns null, then matchesPathPattern() hits and the edge is classed unresolved/no-target.

Impact: one such edge marks import-cycle.density / .groups / .modules incomplete. sloppiness.ts scores an incomplete metric at full weight, so the import-cycle dimension jumped from ~12.8 raw points to 20, and the report became PARTIAL / completeness: incomplete. A Vite app's stylesheet import is standard, so every Vite/React repo hits this.

Required state: when the path mapping substitutes to a file that exists on disk but is not an analyzable source, classify the edge as a resolved non-source asset (not a graph node, not unresolved) so it does not make the graph incomplete. A mapping that substitutes to no existing file stays unresolved.

Acceptance criteria
1. A fixture with a tsconfig paths alias and an aliased .css import produces no graph.unresolved-import finding and graph.edges.unresolved is 0.
2. An aliased import whose target file does not exist is still reported unresolved.
3. Relative asset imports ('./index.css') keep their current behavior; confirm they are already handled and add a test if not.

pivotDisposition.reason: Aliased non-TS asset imports remain a real graph false positive. Conservative incomplete reporting is explicit, not a clean score. Retain the scoped fix and document the release limitation.

title: coverage-budget and file-size-budget safeguards miss enforcement when the check script reads the budget path internally
description:
Observed auditing warren (2026-09-16): coverage-budget and file-size-budget both report 'configured · no CI-reachable check references the budget'. Both are enforced in CI: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs 'bun run check:size' and 'bun run check:coverage:ci'; package.json maps those to 'bun run scripts/check-file-sizes.ts' and 'bun run scripts/check-coverage.ts --junit'; each script resolves its budget file internally (BUDGETS_PATH = resolve(REPO_ROOT, 'scripts/...-budgets.json')).

Root cause: src/safeguards/budgets.ts BUDGET_SPECS uses enforcedBy: body.includes(budgetPath) for both kinds, so enforcement is only seen when the budget path appears literally in a package.json script body or a workflow command. This is the l5-toolkit layout, so every os-eco fleet repo is under-reported the same way. duplication-budget escapes because it matches the jscpd tool name instead.

Required state: follow one hop from a CI-reachable script body to the local script file it runs (extractLocalPaths already finds it) and treat a literal reference to the budget path inside that file as enforcement. Read the file as text only; never import or execute it. Note the evidence chain in the surface notes (script -> file -> budget).

Acceptance criteria
1. A fixture with the l5-toolkit layout (CI -> package script -> scripts/check-*.ts naming the budget JSON) reports structurally-wired for both budgets.
2. A budget file that no CI-reachable script or script file names stays 'configured'.
3. A script file that names the budget but is not CI-reachable stays 'configured'.
4. Safeguards remain outside the score.

pivotDisposition.reason: Indirect budget wiring remains a real safeguard evidence limitation; configuration is reported conservatively and never affects score. Retain the scoped follow-up, carrying forward the tool-independent evidence lesson from trellis-589a.

title: Calibration evidence: absolute-count saturation thresholds pin large repos at a 50-point floor (warren scores 100/100)
description:
Input for trellis-e924 (corpus calibration). Data point from auditing warren at scoring 0.1.0-provisional, 2026-09-16: 894 production files, 121519 sloc, 7375 functions -> index 100/100.

Term trace (value / saturatesAt):
- erosion.eroded-count.production 263 / 20 (13x over)
- erosion.eroded-share.production 0.3041 / 0.25
- duplication.density.production 0.2059 / 0.15
- duplication.groups.production 1381 / 15 (92x over)
- import-cycle.density 0.0278 / 0.10 (27.8 normalized)
- import-cycle.groups 10 / 5
Raw total 92.8; reported 100 because import-cycle was degraded by an unresolved-import false positive (filed separately).

Problem: the count terms (20 eroded functions, 15 clone groups, 5 cycle groups) are repo-size-blind and saturate at values any repo past roughly 10k sloc exceeds. They carry half of every dimension, so every large repo has a floor of 50 regardless of density, and the index has no resolution in the range where real repos live. Once saturated, the term gives zero gradient: warren could remove 1300 clone groups and the term would not move. SPEC 3.4 wants counts retained so clean additions cannot dilute debt; that intent survives a threshold that is reachable, but not one that is always exceeded.

Second observation: duplication.density.production is 20.6 percent here while warren's own jscpd gate passes at a low single-digit threshold. Record the detector settings (min tokens/lines, whether type-only and import blocks count) beside the corpus results so the density threshold is calibrated against what this detector measures, not against jscpd intuition.

Options to evaluate against the corpus: log-scaled count terms; saturation set from corpus percentiles; counts normalized per kloc with a separate non-dilution guard; a smaller share for count terms. Any change bumps SCORING_VERSION and the test expectations together.

Acceptance criteria
1. The corpus record shows where each count term saturates across repo sizes and states whether a size-independent floor is intended.
2. The chosen formula keeps the monotonicity rule and the no-dilution rule from SPEC 7.
3. Repos of clearly different quality at similar size land at visibly different scores.

pivotDisposition.reason: Provisional large-repo saturation remains a calibration limitation, not a completed fix. trellis-e924 calibrates clone size but does not establish broad size invariance. Retain further corpus research outside this bounded release.

title: One non-literal dynamic import() marks the whole dependency graph incomplete and charges the full 20 import-cycle points
description: Found while test-auditing external repos for the 'can you quantify slop' video (2026-09-17). honojs/hono src/ has exactly one unresolved edge (utils/color.ts:48, reason non-literal-dynamic) and pays the full 20 cycle points + PARTIAL. description:

The pinned spike distribution carries conflicting license evidence: eslint-plugin-sonarjs 3.0.5 package metadata and lockfile entry declare LGPL-3.0-only while the shipped LICENSE file and the cognitive-complexity implementation header identify the SONAR Source-Available License v1.0. Package metadata alone does not authorize redistribution, and no agent in this repo may render a legal opinion.

Clearance requires a written determination by an authorized party (a SonarSource licensing clarification or the operator's qualified counsel) that resolves the conflict and establishes a route trellis can lawfully exercise — for example confirmation that the distribution is LGPL-3.0-only with obligations trellis can satisfy, or explicit written permission for the intended use. The determination must be recorded as evidence in this repo (documented terms, date, scope) before any executable support is enabled.
